title: A certified three-equilibrium bound for 375 fixed quadratic zero-one reaction networks

upstream.license_status: not confirmed; no redistribution or relicensing

claims.statement: Each of the fixed 375 networks has at most three distinct positive equilibria for every strictly positive rate vector, including degenerate equilibria.

domain.networks: the exact pinned list, without a new enumeration claim

claims.argument: Cramer reconstruction is injective along the retained coordinate at positive equilibria; removed factors cannot vanish there and residuals never specialize to zero. The second route uses unique positive fibers and a Descartes bound on nonzero retained factors.

claims.statement: Within the fixed list, no inflow and an acyclic unimolecular net-production graph select exactly networks 33449 and 239089.
claims.selection_history: Condition chosen after a 12-network pilot and inspection of eight networks without inflow.
claims.limitation: Not a predictive test, a general structural stability theorem, or a new discovery of the two exceptions.

claims.statement: Network 33449 with added X3 -> 0 at positive rate h has at most three distinct positive equilibria and at most one exponentially stable positive equilibrium for all seven positive rates.
claims.argument: The t reduction is a cubic with strictly negative leading coefficient. At an equilibrium det J=-y Qprime, so exponential stability requires a positive-slope root, of which a cubic with negative leading coefficient has at most one. The z chart supplies a second elimination identity.
claims.limitation: No nonlinear stability claim for degenerate or boundary points.

claims.statement: At the bundled rational rates, the seven-reaction family has exactly three simple positive equilibria; one is exponentially stable and two are unstable.
claims.selection_history: Six rates from a fixed earlier witness; h=1/65536 selected by the recorded dyadic ladder.

not_claimed: a new blind review during packaging

pending_companion_citation.title: Stability certificates for two exceptional reaction networks
